rationale: C05 plausibly supplied material for the child's drafting. It establishes the precise policy process underlying the later letter—a comprehensive review of foreign economic policy intended to produce congressional action—and uses the same integrated rationale linking expanded international trade and private investment to a stronger, self-supporting free world. The child adapts that framework into a defense of the resulting March 30 program and its legislative timetable. C07 closely parallels the appeal for extension of trade-agreements authority and the connection between freer trade and global prosperity, but it is less comprehensive. C03 is a direct procedural antecedent to the March 30 program, though too brief and generic to be the strongest drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a minimum essential program for the building of a stronger America as an integral part of a strong and economically vigorous free world
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the achievement of a strong and self-supporting economic system in the free world...must be a cooperative effort
shared_material.explanation: Both frame foreign economic policy as a means of strengthening the United States through the economic strength of the free world.

shared_material.child_excerpt: raising levels of profitable trade and investment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Through increasing two-way international trade and stimulating in every practical way the flow of private investment abroad we can strengthen the free world
shared_material.explanation: The child compresses C05's paired trade-and-private-investment program into nearly the same policy formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: extension of and amendment of the Trade Agreements Extension Act of 1951, as amended
shared_material.parent_excerpt: requesting a one-year extension of the present Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act...the need for a thorough reexamination of our whole foreign economic policy
shared_material.explanation: C05 supplies the concrete legislative and policy-review framework that culminates in the program defended by the child.
